newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian banks to escape state notes issue penalty.
newsitem.headline: Belgian banks to escape state notes issue penalty.

text.p: The 32 Belgian banks which agreed to market state notes to retail investors on behalf of the Finance Ministry will not be fined after four issues raised less than hoped for in their first year, a Treasury official told Reuters on Tuesday.

"The arrangement was that if more than half of the placing establishments did not reach their agreed quotas we would have to see if there was a problem of a general nature which exempted everyone from a penalty. This is the case," the official said.
"It's clear that there has been little incentive for private savers to invest at fixed rates for an extended period," he said.

The Finance Ministry said on Tuesday its latest issue of state notes had raised 8.65 billion Belgian francs, taking the total sold in the first four issues to 53.25 billion. The banks had agreed to try and place 85.5 billion francs.
The Treasury official said "a little more than 17" of the banks failed to hit their quotas, which were set following a tender held by the Treasury last year.
He noted the banks, against a background of falling long-term interest rates, had had problems selling their own savings bond certificates in the past year.
The state notes were launched last year in head-on competition with bank savings bonds, traditionally Belgium's most popular investment vehicle.
The official said, however, there were no plans to abandon the state notes programme.
"It's a long-term programme. Markets go up and down. It's not like the Philippe (state bond) issues of the past. With the state notes we have decided to be here regularly," he said.
The official said that private banks would shortly be asked to make offers to market next year's four issues, due to start in June. No target figure had yet been arranged for the issues.
He declined to comment on the mechanism the Treasury would have used to penalise banks that failed to meet their quotas.
